title: Non-positive inner product of normalized projections off a unit vector
statement:
Let $u,v,w$ be vectors in a real inner product space with $\norm{u}=1$, and suppose the three inner products $\langle v,w\rangle$, $\langle v,u\rangle$, and $\langle w,u\rangle$ are all nonpositive. For a vector $x$, write $x^{\perp}=x-\langle u,x\rangle\,u$ for its component orthogonal to $u$, and assume that both $v^{\perp}$ and $w^{\perp}$ are nonzero. Then their normalizations still have nonpositive inner product:
\[
\left\langle \frac{v^{\perp}}{\norm{v^{\perp}}},\ \frac{w^{\perp}}{\norm{w^{\perp}}}\right\rangle \le 0.
\]
hypotheses_covered: the orthogonal component of v off u is nonzero
the orthogonal component of w off u is nonzero
replaced:
Under $\norm{u} = 1$, $\langle v,w\rangle \le 0$, $\langle v,u\rangle \le 0$ and
$\langle w,u\rangle \le 0$ (with both projections nonzero), the normalized projections
of $v$ and $w$ also have non-positive inner product.
